instructions: This demonstration has 3 multiple-choice questions and 6 free-response questions on one biology topic. It uses a 7-minute classroom walkthrough clock with a 1-minute break. It is not a full mock examination: the real exam has 60 multiple-choice questions and broader topic coverage. Before starting, your teacher should supply the current AP Biology equations and formulas sheet and a four-function calculator with square root or a scientific nongraphing calculator. For May 2027, handheld graphing calculators and other handheld calculators with storage capabilities are not allowed. Bluebook offers Desmos scientific; DigitalDP uses your supplied calculator. Complete Section I digitally and Section II in the supplied practice booklet or digital canvas. DigitalDP opens the next section automatically after the fixed break.

resources.label: Original population study
resources.text:
Researchers grew a freshwater alga at four nitrate concentrations. Each treatment had six independent cultures.
Nitrate (mg L⁻¹): 0, 2, 5, 10
Mean growth rate (day⁻¹): 0.08, 0.19, 0.31, 0.30
Standard error: 0.01, 0.02, 0.02, 0.03

questions.label: Section I — Question 1
questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the overlap in standard-error ranges at 5 and 10 mg L⁻¹ nitrate?
options: Growth certainly declines above 5 mg L⁻¹
The two means may not differ detectably
All cultures grew at the same rate

questions.label: Section I — Question 2
questions.prompt: Which change would best test whether light limits growth at 10 mg L⁻¹ nitrate?
options: Vary light while holding nitrate constant

questions.label: Section I — Question 3
questions.prompt: The nitrate taken up by the alga is most directly used to synthesize

questions.label: Section II — Question 1: experimental results
questions.prompt: Describe the relationship between nitrate concentration and algal growth, propose a cellular explanation for the plateau, and evaluate whether the data support a causal conclusion.

questions.label: Section II — Question 2: graphing
questions.prompt: Graph the means with correctly labelled axes and error bars. Use the graph to identify a nitrate range for a follow-up treatment and justify the choice.

questions.label: Section II — Question 3: scientific investigation
questions.prompt: Design a follow-up investigation that tests whether light limits growth at 10 mg L⁻¹ nitrate. State the independent variable, controls, replication, measurement and predicted result.

questions.label: Section II — Question 4: conceptual analysis
questions.prompt: Explain how nitrate uptake can affect protein synthesis and therefore population growth in the alga.

questions.label: Section II — Question 5: model analysis
questions.prompt: Construct and label a model showing how nitrate availability, amino-acid synthesis and cell division could produce the observed growth response. Identify one limitation of the model.

questions.label: Section II — Question 6: data analysis
questions.prompt: Calculate the percentage increase in mean growth rate from 0 to 5 mg L⁻¹ nitrate. Use the standard-error values to explain one limitation of comparing only the two means.
